key_insight: COBRA-Skills turns skill optimization for LLM agents into budgeted, sequential search by using contextual-bandit guidance to focus evaluation on the most promising or informative candidate skills.
engineering_relevance: For agent systems, this offers a practical way to improve reusable skills with much lower execution cost, making iterative optimization more feasible under tight evaluation budgets.
method: Prioritize candidate skills with a contextual bandit instead of evaluating all options equally.
Evolve the skill pool using execution feedback, so the candidate space improves over time.
Allocate budget selectively to promising or informative skills rather than relying on large task datasets.
evidence_signal: Across six heterogeneous benchmarks and three target models, the method achieved the strongest average performance while cutting optimization cost by 55–58% versus SkillOpt and using only 50 unique optimization examples per benchmark.
watch_item: Because the framework depends on execution feedback and evolving candidate pools, performance may be sensitive to harness design and reward/feedback quality in new environments.
paper_title: COBRA-Skills: Contextual Bandit-Guided Evolution for Agent Skill Optimization
